description: Excel's Goal Seek on a Svelte 5 spreadsheet grid: a pricing model with three scenarios side by side, and Data > Goal Seek to set the profit cell to a target by changing the price. The solver is a secant method with a bisection fallback. The sheet does not move until the status dialog reports the solution and OK is pressed; OK writes through the grid's command context, so the whole seek is one undo step. Enterprise, in @svgrid/enterprise.

faq.question: How does Goal Seek find the input?
faq.answer: It evaluates the formula cell for trial values of the input cell with a secant step, and falls back to bisection when the secant step leaves the bracket, until the formula lands within tolerance of the target or the iteration limit is hit.

faq.question: Does the sheet change while it searches?
faq.answer: No. The search runs on a scratch evaluation; the status dialog shows the value found, and only OK writes it into the input cell. Cancel leaves the sheet as it was.

faq.question: Is the result one undo step?
faq.answer: Yes. OK writes through the command context, so Ctrl+Z puts the input back in one press.
